description: # **Senior Business Analyst, Product Development** ### **About the product** Most companies still answer business questions the way they did twenty years ago. Someone files a request, an analyst turns it into SQL, and the answer arrives after the decision has moved on. We build an AI analytics platform that ends that wait. A business user asks a question in plain English and gets a correct, charted answer from their organisation's data in seconds, along with the anomalies, forecasts and recommended actions they never thought to ask for. Every answer the AI gives is only as good as the business definitions sitting behind it. ### **The role** You join the product development team, the engineers and analysts who build the platform itself. You own the backlog, turn what clients and the market need into requirements a developer can build from, and decide with the team what earns a place on the roadmap. It is a business analysis role with one difference. The product you specify is an AI. When the output is a button you can write the acceptance criteria in a line. When the output is an answer a model generates, you have to define what correct looks like, design the tests that prove it, and turn every miss into something an engineer can reproduce and fix. title: Lead AI Engineer

The agents translate natural language into T-SQL and DAX over messy enterprise schemas, backed by deterministic query patterns and a governed metric layer for the questions where roughly right is not good enough. - Design the knowledge the agents reason over, including the ontology and knowledge graph that describe a client's schema, entities, business rules and vocabulary, the semantic and metric layer above it, and the retrieval that brings the right piece forward at the right moment. - Push the platform from answering to anticipating, growing the proactive side of the product. description: # **Senior Data Engineer, Client Implementations** ### **About the product** Most companies still answer business questions the way they did twenty years ago. Someone files a request, an analyst turns it into SQL, and the answer arrives after the decision has moved on. We build an AI analytics platform that ends that wait. A business user asks a question in plain English and gets a correct, charted answer from their organisation's data in seconds, along with the anomalies, forecasts and recommended actions they never thought to ask for. Everything the AI knows about a client's business flows from the data platform underneath it. ### **The Role** You join the implementation team, the people who take a new client from a won deal to a live deployment. You sit in the client sessions, work out their business and data requirements, take receipt of their raw source data, and build the medallion architecture the deployment runs on. Your warehouse has an unusual consumer. It is read by an AI agent thousands of times a day, without a human in the loop, and every ambiguity you leave in the model can surface as a confident wrong answer in a chat window. You build data models a language model can read correctly, and that is a higher bar than building for people. ### **What you'll work on** - Join client meetings from kickoff, with their operations people and their IT, and turn what the business means by its own terms into definitions a pipeline can compute. - Take raw source extracts, CRM systems, operational feeds and event logs, and work out their structure, grain and quality yourself. Client data dictionaries are rare and usually wrong. - Build the bronze, silver and gold layers, from ingestion through transform notebooks to a governed gold star schema, with incremental loads, watermarks and freshness you can vouch for. - Encode the client's business logic in the transforms. Typical cases include current state that must be derived from an audit event log with carry-forward rules, identity resolution across parent and child records, and exclusion rules that change what every downstream count means. - Write the data dictionary that feeds the agent, the table and column annotations, grain cards and join paths that become part of what the AI knows about the client. - Prove the numbers are right. Reconcile the gold layer against the client's source reports, run the data-quality , chase every figure that does not tie, and fix the transform rather than the symptom. - Design the row-level security model at the data layer, so the same warehouse serves different user scopes safely. - Make each new client faster than the last, hardening the ingestion and modelling playbook so onboarding becomes repeatable. ### **What we're looking for** - A senior track record in data engineering, with warehouses or lakehouses you built running in production and being relied on. - Expert SQL and strong Python, including PySpark or a similar large-scale transform stack. - Real depth in dimensional modelling. You think in grains, conformed dimensions and slowly changing state, and you can derive current state correctly from an event log. - You are comfortable in front of a client. You can sit with business stakeholders, ask the questions that surface what they actually mean, and hold your own when their numbers disagree with yours. - A reconciliation habit. You have owned the correctness of a data platform, you assume the numbers do not tie until proven otherwise, and you have the patience to find out why. - You can take an undocumented source system and map it yourself, without waiting for someone to explain it. ### **Nice to have** Microsoft Fabric or Delta Lake, the Azure ecosystem, complex CRM or operational source systems, dbt or a similar transform framework, data-quality tooling, Power BI, and experience feeding data to LLM or ML systems. ### **How we work** Small senior team, remote, with direct access to the end clients and the problems they need solved.
